problems.title: A product inequality becomes a double-angle inequality
problems.question: Solve sinx cosx>1/4.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: $2\sin x\cos x=\sin2x$.
steps: Require sin2x>1/2, so 2x∈(π/6+2πk,5π/6+2πk). Divide by 2.

problems.title: Principal inverse-sine value
problems.question: Evaluate arcsin(sin5), with angles in radians.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: The range of arcsin is $[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$.
steps: 5−2π lies in this interval and has the same sine as 5. Thus the value is 5−2π.

problems.title: Least positive root after a tangent substitution
problems.question: Solve 4sin²x−sin2x=3 and find the least positive root.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: cosx=0 gives 4≠3, so divide by cos²x and put t=tanx.
steps: All roots are x=arctan3+kπ or x=−π/4+kπ. Their least positive representatives are arctan3 and 3π/4; arctan3 is smaller.
problems.answer: Least positive root $\arctan3$; full roots $x=\arctan3+k\pi$ or $-\pi/4+k\pi$.

problems.title: Regular triangular pyramid lateral area
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has lateral edges 5 and height 3. Find lateral surface area.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: The base circumradius satisfies $R^2=5^2-3^2$; an equilateral base has side R√3.
steps: R=4 and base side=4√3. Each lateral triangle’s altitude is √(25−(2√3)²)=√13.
Three face areas total 3×(1/2)×4√3×√13=6√39.

problems.title: A cube section parallel to an edge
problems.question: Which nondegenerate polygon can arise from a cube section by a plane parallel to at least one cube edge?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: Choose that edge direction as the vertical axis; the plane equation is independent of the vertical coordinate.
steps: The section is the product of a line segment across the base square with the full vertical edge interval. It is a rectangle, hence a quadrilateral.
Degenerate touching sections can be points or segments, but no other polygon type occurs.

problems.title: Two sine arguments
problems.question: Solve sin5x=sin(−3x).
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: $\sin5x+\sin3x=2\sin4x\cos x$.
steps: sin4x=0 gives x=kπ/4. cosx=0 gives x=π/2+kπ, already included in the first family.

problems.title: Intersect two trigonometric root sets
problems.question: Solve 2sin²x−3sinx+1=0 and 4cos²x+2(√3−1)cosx−√3=0, in degrees.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: The first factors as (2sinx−1)(sinx−1); the second has cosine roots 1/2 and −√3/2.
steps: sinx=1 has cosine 0 and fails the second equation. For sinx=1/2, the possible cosines are ±√3/2, and only the negative one is allowed.
Thus x is 150° modulo 360°.

problems.title: A closed cosine inequality
problems.question: Solve cosx≤−√2/2.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: On a unit-circle cycle cosine is at most −√2/2 between 3π/4 and 5π/4.
steps: Include both boundary angles and repeat every 2π.

problems.title: Square pyramid height from lateral area
problems.question: A regular square pyramid has base side 2 and lateral area 5. Find height.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: Lateral area $=Pl/2$ with slant height l; $l^2=H^2+(s/2)^2$.

problems.title: Equal face inclinations and projected areas
problems.question: A pyramid’s trapezoid base has midline 3 and inradius 1. Every lateral face makes 60° with the base. Find lateral area.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: Trapezoid height is 2r; orthogonal projection of each face scales area by cos60°.
steps: Base area=midline×height=3×2=6. The apex projection is the common incenter, so face projections partition the base.
Thus lateral area×cos60°=6, giving lateral area=12.

problems.title: A trigonometric product’s domain
problems.question: Solve cosx tanx=0.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: Tangent requires cosx≠0; on that domain cosx tanx=sinx.
steps: Thus sinx=0 gives x=kπ. These all have nonzero cosine. The excluded cosine zeros cannot be counted as product roots.

problems.title: Largest negative solution of a shifted sine
problems.question: Find the largest negative root of 4sinx+3cosx=1.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: $4\sin x+3\cos x=5\sin(x+\varphi)$ with $\varphi=\arctan(3/4)$.
steps: Let t=arcsin(1/5). Solutions are x=t−φ+2πk or x=π−t−φ+2πk.
Since 0<t<φ<π/2, the first family’s k=0 value is negative and closest to zero. The second family’s nearest negative value is −π−t−φ, smaller.

problems.title: Count integer roots after using secant squared
problems.question: How many integer x∈[−π,0] satisfy (2+2tan²x)cosx+1<0?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: On cosx≠0, the left side simplifies to $2/\cos x+1$.
steps: It is negative exactly when cosx<0, because 0<|cosx|≤1. The integers in [−π,0] are −3,−2,−1,0.
Only −3 and −2 have negative cosine.

problems.title: Plane-section polygons of a tetrahedron
problems.question: Which polygon types can a nondegenerate plane section of a tetrahedron have?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: Each of four faces can contribute at most one boundary segment.
steps: At most four sides are possible. A plane near a vertex gives a triangle; one separating two vertices from the other two gives a quadrilateral.

problems.title: A square-frustum diagonal section
problems.question: A regular square frustum has base sides √2,3√2. Its diagonal-section diagonals are perpendicular. Find that section area.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: The section is an isosceles trapezoid with bases 2,6. Its diagonal horizontal components are ±(2+6)/2=±4.
steps: Perpendicularity gives height²=4², so section height=4. Area=(2+6)×4/2=16.

problems.title: A tangent value on a fixed interval
problems.question: For which a does tanx=2a−1 have a root in [0,π/4]?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: Tangent increases continuously from 0 to 1 on this interval.
steps: Require 0≤2a−1≤1, giving 1/2≤a≤1. Both endpoints correspond to allowed x endpoints.

problems.title: Bounds rule out every solution
problems.question: Find a first-quadrant solution of −sin²(0.8x)+sin(0.8x)=tan²(0.1x)−4tan(0.1x)+6.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
steps: The left side is always at most 1/4 and the right always at least 2 wherever defined. They cannot be equal in any quadrant.

problems.title: Trigonometric functions of inverse values
problems.question: Evaluate sin(arctan(2√2))+tan(arcsin√0.1).
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: For t>0, $\sin(\arctan t)=t/\sqrt{1+t^2}$; $\tan(\arcsin u)=u/\sqrt{1-u^2}$.
steps: The first term is 2√2/3. The second is √(0.1/0.9)=1/3. Their sum is (2√2+1)/3.

problems.title: Square pyramid from a lateral dihedral angle
problems.question: A regular square pyramid has base side √6 and internal dihedral angle 120° between adjacent lateral faces. Find lateral area.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: For base side s,height H, adjacent outward face normals have cosine $(s^2/4)/(H^2+s^2/4)$.
steps: The outward-normal angle supplements the internal dihedral, so it is 60°. Set that cosine to 1/2, giving H²=s²/4.
The face slant height is √(H²+s²/4)=s/√2=√3. Lateral area=2s·l=2√6√3=6√2.

problems.title: Triangular-frustum face inclination
problems.question: A regular triangular frustum has base circumradii 2,8 and lateral edge 3√5. Find angle between a lateral face and the base.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: Height² = edge² minus circumradius-difference²; an equilateral base’s apothem is half its circumradius.
steps: Height=√(45−36)=3. The face’s horizontal inward run is the apothem difference (8−2)/2=3.
Thus tanθ=3/3=1, giving θ=45°.

problems.title: An equation is an identity on its restricted domain
problems.question: Solve [((sinx+cosx)²−1)²](cos⁴x−sin⁴x)^(−2)=[1−cos4x]/[1+cos4x].
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: $(\sin x+\cos x)^2-1=\sin2x$; $\cos^4x-\sin^4x=\cos2x$.
steps: The left is tan²2x. The right is also tan²2x by half-angle identities.
The original denominators require cos2x≠0, excluding x=π/4+kπ/2. Every other real x satisfies the identity.

problems.title: Sign chart for a sine sum
problems.question: Solve sin3x+sin5x≤0 for x∈(0,3π/2).
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: $\sin3x+\sin5x=2\sin4x\cos x$.
steps: Use the zeros kπ/4 of sin4x and π/2,3π/2 of cosine. Their sign chart makes the product nonpositive on [π/4,3π/4] and [π,5π/4].
All listed endpoints are inside the original open interval and give zero, so they are included.

problems.title: A quadratic in a principal inverse sine
problems.question: For which a does (arcsinx)²−(a+1)π arcsinx+aπ²=0 have exactly one solution?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
formulas: Put t=arcsinx∈[−π/2,π/2]; the equation factors $(t-\pi)(t-a\pi)=0$.
steps: t=π is outside the principal range. The only possible root is t=aπ, allowed exactly when −1/2≤a≤1/2.
Sine is one-to-one on the principal interval, so each allowed a gives exactly one x=sin(aπ).

problems.title: A plane through two incentres and a circumcentre
problems.question: A pyramid has right-isosceles base ABC, legs 6,right angle C, and altitude DC=8. E,F are incentres of ACD,BCD and P circumcentre of ABC. At what height does plane EFP meet DC?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
steps: The side triangles are 6–8–10 right triangles, each with inradius (6+8−10)/2=2. Thus E=(2,0,2),F=(0,2,2).
The base circumcentre is hypotenuse midpoint P=(3,3,0). Their plane is x+y+2z=6.
On DC, x=y=0, so z=3. The intersection is height 3 above the base plane.

problems.title: A cube plane divides an edge
problems.question: In unit cube ABCDA₁B₁C₁D₁, M is midpoint BC,N midpoint AA₁,and K∈D₁C₁ with D₁K:KC₁=1:3. Find the ratio in which MNK cuts A₁D₁.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard equation or cross-section, retaining the original restrictions.
steps: M=(1,1/2,0),N=(0,0,1/2),K=(1/4,1,1). Their plane is 12x−10y+14z=7, verified by substitution.
On A₁D₁, x=0,z=1, giving y=7/10. The two edge pieces from A₁ and D₁ are 7/10,3/10.
